gloss: highest score; highest point; maximum mark

definitions.gloss: highest score; top mark; maximum points
definitions.explanation: The best or highest score achieved in a test, competition, or evaluation. Commonly used in academic and competitive contexts.
The physically or figuratively highest point of something, such as the peak of a mountain range or the pinnacle of a career.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}のテストの{最高点|さいこうてん}は98{点|てん}だった。
examples.english: The highest score on this test was 98 points.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はクラスで{最高点|さいこうてん}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: She got the top score in the class.

examples.japanese: {全教科|ぜんきょうか}で{最高点|さいこうてん}を{目指|めざ}すのは{現実的|げんじつてき}ではない。
examples.english: Aiming for the top score in every subject is not realistic.

examples.japanese: この{山脈|さんみゃく}の{最高点|さいこうてん}は3,000メートルを{超|こ}える。
examples.english: The highest point of this mountain range exceeds 3,000 meters.

examples.japanese: {株価|かぶか}が{過去|かこ}{最高点|さいこうてん}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: Stock prices reached an all-time high.

examples.japanese: {選手生活|せんしゅせいかつ}の{最高点|さいこうてん}は{世界|せかい}{選手権|せんしゅけん}での{金|きん}メダルだった。
examples.english: The peak of his athletic career was the gold medal at the world championship.

notes:
Composed of {最高|さいこう} (highest; best) and {点|てん} (point; score). The academic sense is by far the most common in everyday use. In Japanese schools, test scores are a frequent topic of conversation, and {最高点|さいこうてん} appears regularly in school announcements and discussions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最高点|さいこうてん}を{取|と}る: to get the highest score
- {最高点|さいこうてん}を{記録|きろく}する: to record the highest score
- {過去|かこ}{最高点|さいこうてん}: all-time high score/point

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最低点|さいていてん}: lowest score/point — the opposite
- {満点|まんてん}: perfect score — the maximum possible score, not just the best achieved
- {最高|さいこう}: highest; the best — the broader adjective/noun without the specific 'point/score' meaning
